summary: Attacked the Commutative algebra area: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra (9 stages), HabiroCyclotomicCompletions (6) and HabiroRings (8). No finding. Every stage prerequisite resolves, and the atlas has no unresolved non-sentinel requires at all; the six restructuring proposals that touch the area never act on the same layer twice; no mathematics is planned twice among the three roadmaps or against the wider Habiro family; every stage reference in the 24 source routes that reach the area resolves; and everything the three roadmaps plan is genuinely absent from the pinned libraries. Two structures that look like defects are measured and explained below rather than reported, so that the next reader does not raise them.
checked: All three roadmaps and their documents: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra's 9 stages in two id families, R03.1 to R03.6 and P7 to P9; HabiroCyclotomicCompletions's 6; HabiroRings's 8.

Prerequisite resolution. Every `requires` entry of the area's 23 stages resolves to a real stage, with one exception that is house practice: HC.1 requires UPSTREAM:Polynomial-cyclotomic-completion-algebra, and UPSTREAM sentinels appear in the `requires` of 76 stages across 29 roadmaps. Measured for context: the atlas has zero unresolved non-sentinel `requires` anywhere, so the graph is fully resolved and this area is not an exception to anything. The roadmap-level prerequisites and consumers of all three also resolve, including HabiroRings's eight prerequisites and the nine consumers of the deformation roadmap.

The first structure that looks like a defect and is not: HabiroRings:HR.5 and HabiroRings:HR.5-number-field-comparison carry byte-identical descriptions, although their titles and `requires` differ, so the sub-stage appears to have no text of its own. That is the atlas extraction's universal handling of a sub-stage anchor inside a parent section, not a defect of this roadmap: the README places inside the ## HR.5 section, and across the atlas 119 of 1962 stages share a description with a sibling, in HabiroCohomologyFoundations, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves, K2SymbolsBrauer, MotivicEtaleKTheory, StableHomotopyKTheory, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory and others.

The second: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra mixes two id families, which looked like a merge artefact. It is not. Its own README carries ## R03.1 to ## R03.6 and then ## P7, ## P8 and ## P9 as separate sections, so both lanes are the document's. The keys P7, P8 and P9 are also used by PadicHodgeTheory and PerfectoidSpaces, but stage ids are roadmap-qualified, so there is no collision.

Duplication among the three roadmaps and against the whole six-roadmap Habiro family (AnalyticHabiroStack, HabiroCohomologyFoundations, HabiroCyclotomicCompletions, HabiroNahmSeries, HabiroNumberFields, HabiroRings), by a term-overlap comparison of all 55 stages in scope. Twelve candidate pairs cross a 0.30 threshold and every one of them is between HabiroNumberFields and HabiroNahmSeries, neither of which is in this area, and all twelve share the readiness-checkpoint boilerplate rather than any mathematics. Nothing involving the three roadmaps of this area is planned twice.

The six restructuring proposals that name the area — RS-05, RS-08, RS-10, RS-16, RS-18 and RS-33 — for conflicting actions on one layer, which no single proposal's own review would catch. Twenty layers and roadmaps of the area are acted on, and every one is acted on by exactly one proposal: RS-08 narrows P7, R03.1 and R03.3 and keeps the roadmap, RS-10 keeps or narrows all of HC.1 to HC.6 and HR.1 to HR.7. No layer is narrowed twice and no two proposals disagree.

The 24 source routes that reach the area from paper extractions, carrying 48 stage references between them: every reference resolves to a real stage. The deformation roadmap alone is a source for 21 extractions, among them Calegari-Geraghty, Iyengar-Khare-Manning, Le-Le Hung-Levin and four Boxer-Calegari-Gee-Pilloni papers.

What the three roadmaps plan against the pinned libraries. Habiro rings, cyclotomic completions, Schlessinger's criterion, deformation functors, complete-intersection criteria, patching and Taylor-Wiles systems each have zero declarations at the pin, so they are rightly planned; perfect complexes, which P7 builds on, do exist, which is consistent with P7 being a derived-coefficient-change layer rather than a construction of perfect complexes.

One omission probe, since WORKERS.md lists the Koszul complex among the notions the libraries lack and section 15 requires such a notion to be planned once in the roadmap that owns it. The Koszul complex is planned, by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6 ('Build Koszul/Buchsbaum-Rim complexes, their grade/regularity hypotheses, exactness'). This area does not mention it, and I did not report that as a gap: its depth theory is planned directly in R03.3 as 'regular sequences, depth, Cohen-Macaulay rings/modules, projective dimension, Auslander-Buchsbaum and the exact complete-intersection criteria used in patching', which does not require the Koszul complex, and inventing a dependency the roadmap does not state would not be a finding.
